statement.en: ESGE recommends the best practice submucosal injection technique described below for hot snare EMR.

text.en: Do not attempt to lift the whole lesion at once. Start by lifting only the part you will start to resect, then follow a process of sequential injection and resection for larger lesions.
Use injection to improve lesion access and visualization ([Fig. 2], image B2).
Ensure air is expelled from the injection catheter prior to the first injection (priming).

Injection through clearly benign lesions is acceptable if necessary ([Fig. 2], image B1). Caution should be exercised when attempting injection through lesions suspected of containing SMIC because of the risk of malignant seeding [111].

Injection should be performed dynamically. The injection is started (short stab, tangential to the mucosa) as the tissue is being punctured and then the catheter is pulled back and lifted up/away in the desired direction [112].
Avoid intramucosal blebs (intramucosal injection) ([Fig. 2], image B4). If these occur, puncture them and re-attempt submucosal injection [113].
Stop the injection if no lifting is noted (likely transmural/intraperitoneal injection).
Obtain an appropriate and sustained lifting of the lesion ([Fig. 2], image B2).
Do not over-lift, especially in narrow segments (e. g. sigmoid colon) or at flexures.
